elements.element: Vendor (Servicer/Marketing Agent) indemnifies Customer against third-party IP infringement claims regarding services/deliverables
elements.evidence: will indemnify the Issuer against any third-party claim that the systems, software, reports or other deliverables it provides ... infringe any intellectual property right
except to the extent the claim arises from modifications made by the Issuer

elements.element: Exclusion for combinations with items not supplied by Vendor
elements.evidence: the Issuer's combination of those items with items not supplied by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent

elements.element: Remedy: procure the right to continue use
elements.evidence: will procure the right to continue using the affected item
or modify ... it so that it is non-infringing
or ... replace it so that it is non-infringing
refund the fees paid for the affected item

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: will not exceed 3x the annual fees payable to it under the Transaction Documents

elements.element: Vendor duty to defend (in addition to indemnify)
elements.evidence: clause says only 'will indemnify the Issuer'; no defence obligation added
indemnity runs only to 'the Issuer' in clause (iii)

elements.element: Indemnity for Vendor's breach of law
elements.evidence: no breach-of-law trigger anywhere in Section 6.3

elements.element: Indemnity for data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: no data breach trigger in the clause
resulting from the Servicer's ... willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence
(b) Proceedings ... promptly notify ... may participate in and assume the defense and settlement; no cooperation covenant

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: no Customer indemnity exists in the clause, so the condition is absent

reasons: The inserted clause (iii) completes every atomic element of the fallback: a Vendor-side IP infringement indemnity, the three customary exclusions (modification, combination, specification), all four remedies (procure/modify/replace/refund) and an express 3× annual fees super-cap.
Preferred is not met: no express duty to defend, no affiliate coverage, and no breach-of-law or Vendor-caused data breach triggers; the drafter's locked target was fallback, so this is acceptable.

Minimal: a single concise insertion filling an absent IP indemnity, with no rewrite of the existing willful misconduct/bad faith/gross negligence indemnities or the Proceedings mechanic; 'severally and not jointly' is necessary given two distinct indemnitors.

Intent preserved: the existing notice/defence-assumption procedure in (b) applies to the new indemnity without contradiction, and the cap is expressly confined to clause (iii) so it does not dilute the existing uncapped indemnities.
